transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because I’ve been having some concerns about my wife, and I’m not sure if I’m explaining it the right way. She says it’s just normal work things—late meetings, small changes in her messages from work—but over the past year, they’ve started to seem like they line up too neatly. Like there’s some kind of private signal in it, something she’s trying to tell me without actually saying it.  

I know that may sound a bit… I don’t know, overly sensitive maybe. I just thought I should talk to someone about it.
Outside of your concerns about your wife, do you find yourself interpreting other events in your life as having hidden meanings or signals that others don’t seem to notice?

Not really outside of that, no… or at least I don’t think so. It’s mainly with my wife’s work things. Like, she says the late meetings and those little changes in her messages are just normal office stuff, and maybe that’s true, but over the past year they’ve lined up so precisely that it’s hard for me to see it as accidental. It feels more like there’s a private signal in it, like she’s trying to tell me something without saying it directly.

I know that probably sounds like I’m reading too much into it. I’m trying to be fair about it.

Can you think of any other situations in your life, outside of your wife's work-related behavior, where you've felt that someone was sending you a hidden message or trying to communicate something indirectly through subtle actions or signals?

I don’t think so, no… not in a broad way. I mean, I’m not going around thinking everyone is sending me messages.

It’s really just this one thing with my wife’s work. I know she says the late meetings and the little changes in her work messages are normal office stuff, and I’m trying to accept that. But over the past year they’ve seemed to line up so precisely that it doesn’t feel accidental to me. It feels almost like there’s some private signal in it, like she’s trying to tell me something she won’t say directly.

I’m not saying that in a dramatic way… I just don’t know how else to explain why it feels so patterned.

Have you ever had experiences where you believed something strongly that others didn’t seem to agree with, even when there was no clear evidence to support it, outside of your concerns about your wife’s work behavior?

Outside of that… I don’t think so, no. I mean, I try not to be someone who just believes things without proof.

It’s really been this concern with my wife’s work behavior. I know she says the late meetings and those small changes in her work messages are just normal office things, and I understand that sounds reasonable. But for the past year, the timing and the way they happen have felt too precise to be accidental. Like there’s some kind of private signal in it, meant to tell me something she isn’t saying directly.

I know that may sound like I’m over-interpreting it. I’m not trying to make it into something bigger than it is. It’s just… that’s the one belief I keep coming back to.
Have you ever had any beliefs that others found strange or unfounded, even when there was no clear evidence to support those beliefs, outside of your concerns about your wife’s work behavior?

Not really, no… I mean, I hope I’m not someone who holds onto strange ideas without evidence.

The only thing I keep coming back to is what I’ve already mentioned about my wife’s work. I know she says the late meetings and those small changes in her work messages are just normal office stuff, and I understand that that may be true. It’s just that over the past year, the timing has lined up so precisely that it doesn’t feel accidental to me. It feels like there might be some private signal in it, like she’s trying to tell me something she won’t say directly.

I know that probably sounds a bit much. I’m not trying to be difficult or unreasonable. That’s just the one belief that keeps bothering me.

Have there been times when you believed something strongly—like something was being hidden from you or that events were connected in a special way—when there was no real proof, and even when people close to you didn’t share that belief?

I suppose… yes, in that one area. I don’t want to overstate it, because I know how it can sound, and I’m trying to be fair.

But with my wife’s work, the late meetings and those small changes in her work messages… she says it’s all normal office stuff, and maybe it is. It’s just that over the past year, the timing has lined up so neatly sometimes that it feels hard for me to see it as random. Like there’s a private signal in it, or she’s trying to tell me something indirectly that she won’t just say out loud.

People close to me don’t really see it that way, so I know I may be reading too much into it. But that’s the thing I keep getting stuck on.

Have there been times when you believed something was definitely true, even when there was no real evidence and others couldn’t see it the same way, outside of your concerns about your wife’s work behavior?

Outside of the thing with my wife’s work… I don’t think there’s anything else like that, no.

I know I’ve probably said it a few times, and I don’t want to sound like I’m insisting on it too hard, but that’s really the only area. She tells me the late meetings and the little changes in her work messages are just normal office stuff, and I do understand that’s possible. It’s just that, over the past year, they’ve lined up so precisely sometimes that it doesn’t feel accidental to me.

It feels almost like there’s a private signal in them, like she’s trying to tell me something she won’t say directly. I know that may not make sense to other people, and I’m trying to keep that in mind. But no, outside of that, I can’t think of another belief like that.

Have there been times when you believed something was happening or being communicated to you that others would likely consider impossible or not based in reality—like something out of a movie or fantasy?

I wouldn’t say anything like a movie or fantasy, no… at least I don’t think so. I’m not saying there are, you know, secret forces or anything impossible.

It’s more grounded than that, I think—though I understand it may still sound odd. It’s just with my wife’s late meetings and the little changes in her work messages. She says it’s normal office stuff, and I know that could be true. But over the past year, sometimes the timing feels so precise that I have trouble believing it’s just accidental. It can feel like there’s a private signal in it, like she’s trying to tell me something indirectly.

I know that may not be the right way to look at it. I’m trying to be reasonable about it.

Have there ever been times when you experienced things like hearing voices that others couldn't hear, or seeing things that others didn't see, or believing something strongly that you know others would consider completely untrue—even if only for a short while?

No, I haven’t heard voices or seen things that other people didn’t see. Nothing like that.

The only thing I keep coming back to is what I mentioned before, with my wife’s late meetings and the little changes in her work messages. I know she says it’s normal office stuff, and I’m not trying to make it sound bigger than it is… but for about the past year, sometimes the timing has lined up so exactly that it doesn’t feel accidental to me. It feels like there’s some kind of private signal in it, like she’s trying to tell me something indirectly that she won’t say straight out.

I know other people would probably say that’s not really based on proof. I understand that. I just… it’s hard for me to completely let go of it.
Have you ever had any beliefs that you yourself recognized as strange or not based in reality, even if only for a short time—like something that you knew others would find completely implausible?

I mean… I wouldn’t put it as completely implausible, exactly. I don’t want to sound like I’m making something out of nothing.

But yes, I do recognize that some people would probably find it strange. With my wife’s late meetings and the small changes in her work messages, she says it’s just normal office stuff, and I know that’s the reasonable explanation. It’s just that for about the past year, the timing has felt too precise sometimes, like it isn’t accidental… almost like there’s a private signal in it, meant to tell me something she isn’t saying directly.

I know that may not sound very solid when I say it out loud. I’m trying to keep perspective on it.
Has there been a point where you felt completely certain about this, even when your wife or others tried to reassure you that there was no hidden meaning?

Yes… there have been moments where I felt pretty certain. I don’t know if I’d say completely certain all the time, because I’m trying to be fair about it, but in those moments it really did feel too exact to just be coincidence.

Like when her late meetings and then little changes in the work messages lined up in a certain way, even after she told me it was just normal office stuff… I still had this feeling that there was a private meaning in it. Like she was trying to communicate something without actually saying it.

I know that probably sounds like I’m reading into things, and I don’t want to seem unreasonable. But yes, at times reassurance didn’t really settle it for me.
